v1_kept_intact.rule: v1 is never edited. v2 = v1 plus a list of additions held in lexicon_v2.py. A switch picks v1 or v2.

allowed_sources.a: the canonical colloquialism map in CLAUDE.md (Clarification 6), including closed surface variants of those phrases: tense/person/-ing inflection, hyphenation ('practice-makes-perfect'), and the plain noun of the phrase's key word ('attention' from 'Paying attention')
allowed_sources.b: the verbs of the ten authoritative Noetic definitions: 'affinity for', 'attracted toward', 'adverse to', 'repelled by', 'resonates with', 'impregnated with', 'triggers', 'brought to Mind', and their closed inflections ('resonant' from 'resonates')
allowed_sources.c: domain words for P/C/E/O found in docs/CAS_FOUNDATIONAL_CLARIFICATIONS.md
allowed_sources.d: words observed in the 99 DEV rows (cas-synthetic/data/l4_split/real_dev_unparseables_99.jsonl)

admission_rule.forbidden_source: the sealed 98 (real_heldout_unparseables_98.jsonl). Never opened to pick, test, or tune a word. It is scored exactly once, at the end, count only, with its sha256 checked before and after.
admission_rule.every_alias_carries: a source tag (one or more of a/b/c/d), the target (Noetic number or domain letter), the tier, and for a Noetic alias a written colloquialism-test line: the natural colloquialism for the phrase and the canonical map entry it matches.
admission_rule.noetic_alias_test: Colloquialism test (Clarification 6): the natural colloquialism must match the canonical map entry of exactly one Noetic. Anti-drift: no analytical / audit / scrutinize / find-flaws word may map to ^3 (that is ^6); no reasoning / inference / deduction / causal-analysis word may map to ^8 (that is ^6 + ^9); a landing word ('realization') maps to ^9, never ^8. A source-d Noetic alias is NOT filtered by DEV gold labels: the canonical definition governs, and a DEV row whose writer used the word against its canon meaning is reported as a MISMATCH, not hidden.
admission_rule.domain_word_test: Clarifications names the four domains only as Principled / Cognitive / Evaluative / Operational, so source c adds nothing beyond v1. A source-d domain word is admitted only if (i) it is a plain-English gloss of exactly one domain name, and (ii) in every DEV row where it appears inside a numbered segment, that segment's gold cell has that same domain. A word that fails (ii) in even one DEV row is refused.
admission_rule.bare_noun_tier: A bare noun alias (not a verb frame) goes in the lowest tier (noun_tier), so any verb-frame hit in the same segment decides. Two different bare-noun Noetics in one segment stay AMBIGUOUS; v2 does not break ties.
admission_rule.no_rule_changes: v2 changes only word lists. Segmentation, hedges, polarity, leakage, number words, the verb-frame-first rule and the MATCH/MISMATCH comparison are v1's, unchanged.

dev_baseline_v1.note: 0 of 99 parse under v1 by construction: the DEV rows are half of the 197 v1-unparseable headline rows.

builder_reading_of_the_gaps: Most NO_STATE gaps are surface variants of canon phrases the v1 regexes miss: 'practice-makes-perfect' (hyphenated), 'practice making perfect', bare 'practice/practiced/practice-based', 'attention' without 'paying', 'drawn toward' / 'draws you toward', 'resonant', 'realization', 'thought' without 'a', 'pushed-away'. Many NO_DOMAIN rows are NOT vocabulary gaps: the English simply never names a domain ('a thought about wisdom and insight'); no admissible word can fix those. AMBIGUOUS rows mostly carry two canon phrases in one segment ('an aversion that struck a chord'); a word list cannot fix those either.

predicted_lift_dev_99.honesty_note: A range, written before the v2 code exists. Every row that becomes parseable becomes either MATCH or MISMATCH; some DEV English contradicts its own gold (e.g. 'drawn to you in cognitive thinking' with gold ^2^O), so v2 WILL create new MISMATCH rows. Both numbers are reported.

sealed_98.plan: one scoring pass after lexicon_v2.py is committed; counts only (MATCH / MISMATCH / UNPARSEABLE); no row text printed or stored; sha256 checked before and after the pass. The 481/439 tabulation also covers these 98 rows; it runs once, after the lexicon is frozen, and is not used to change any word.
